description: This case study looks at the health and safety risks faced by the people who handled waste after the April 2015 Gorkha earthquake in Nepal, while recovery was still under way. Gabriella Santi Kasabdji, Piyush Pradhananga and Mohamed ElZomor of Florida International University presented it at the Construction Research Congress 2020 of the American Society of Civil Engineers. The authors note that the main shock and aftershocks damaged many districts and produced large amounts of hazardous waste, such as materials containing lead and mercury, and that many local volunteers handled it without training or knowledge of personal protective equipment. The paper identifies the major health and safety issues in disaster waste management practice in Nepal and argues for giving training priority. The conference paper is available online for purchase from ASCE, and its abstract is free in OpenAlex. Coverage is the earthquake-affected districts. Caveats: the evidence is qualitative and the abstract does not give data sources or numbers. Simulation uses: worker exposure and training constraints for scenarios of debris clearance after earthquakes in developing countries. Related records: the Nepal 2015 tertiary hospital resilience study (case_study-nepal-2015-earthquake-tertiary-hospital-resilience) covers another service affected by the same earthquake.
